observation_summary: The BisectionSolver.solve(f, min, max, initial) method throws a NullPointerException because it incorrectly delegates to a version of solve() that relies on an uninitialized member variable 'f' instead of using the provided function 'f'.
hypothesis: The method solve(UnivariateRealFunction f, double min, double max, double initial) is incorrectly calling solve(min, max) instead of calling the overloaded solve(f, min, max). The solve(min, max) method expects the class member 'f' to be initialized, which it is not in this context, leading to a NullPointerException.
prediction: The code in BisectionSolver.java at line 72 will be changed from 'return solve(min, max);' to 'return solve(f, min, max);'.
experiment_rationale: The stack trace points to the solve method. The bug report explicitly states that the method calls the wrong overload, causing a NullPointerException due to an uninitialized member variable. Changing the call to the correct overload that accepts the function 'f' will resolve the dependency on the uninitialized member.
reasoning_summary: This is an Interface/O-O Messages defect because the method is calling the wrong interface signature (the one that relies on internal state) instead of the one that accepts the required parameter (the function 'f'). It is not an Algorithm/Method issue because the logic of the solver itself is fine; it is simply being invoked via the wrong contract/signature.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not a flaw in the bisection algorithm itself, but a failure to correctly route the call to the appropriate method signature.
